text: dsh-token-plugin 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的用量与费用面板。它监听模型调用并记录 token 用量，在概览、日历和明细中呈现费用与使用情况；设置页还可导出 CSV、JSON 或 PNG 报告。适合希望查看 DSH 模型调用消耗并整理本地账目的用户。用量记录保存在本机；刷新价格目录或订阅汇率时会请求公开数据源。

dsh-token-plugin adds a DSH web panel that records token usage from model calls and shows costs in overview, calendar, and detail views. Users can export CSV, JSON, or PNG reports. Usage records stay local; refreshing public pricing or exchange-rate data requires network access.
想按模型查看 DSH 每次调用用了多少 token、花了多少费用。
我想用日历按天检查模型调用和用量变化。
I need to export my DSH usage and cost records as a report.
用量与费用统计：插件监听 DSH 模型调用并记录上报的 token 用量，面板按概览、日历和明细展示记录；设置页可导出 CSV、JSON 或 PNG。
本地记录保存：用量记录写入专用数据目录，并在面板中提供数据目录、导入与导出入口，便于跨会话查看和整理历史。

dsh-token-plugin README · Overview：dsh-usage-plugin is a **usage & cost tracker** plugin in the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem (a DSH plugin shipped as a Host + Client two-in-one package). After installation, the **"Usage & Cost"** tab appear in the Web UI, right after "Conversation" and "Trace":

dsh-token-plugin README · Overview：> Supports **Windows / macOS / Linux**: paths are handled per platform (`node:path`), and the folder picker / "reveal in file manager" use each OS's native mechanism (macOS: `osascript` / `open`; Linux: `zenity` / `xdg-open`). Export does not depend on Windows-only commands.

dsh-token-plugin README · Overview：- **Usage & Cost**: records each model call's token usage and cache hits (input miss / cache hit / cache write / output / reasoning / finish reason), and computes cost using DeepSeek's peak/valley or base pricing (peak hours on weekdays are automatically priced by Beijing time 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00; since 2026-08-23 weekends are billed entirely at the off-peak rate; since 2026-09-10 12:00 Beijing time the post-V4.1-Flash peak/valley prices apply — `deepseek-flash` off-peak cache hit 0.02 / input 1 / output 4 CNY, peak at twice that). Model names come from the actual request parameters, so non-DeepSeek models are shown truthfully instead of "unknown model"; models without an official price are counted as 0. The overview shows a by-model table plus a by-API-provider × model drill-down (each provider grouped with every model's calls and peak/off-peak cost split) and a grand total row. The overview also supports **date filtering** (Today / Last 7 days / Last 30 days / All, plus a custom start–end range), so the aggregate stats can be scoped to any single day or date range.

```bash

```

Alternatively, install a locally packed checkout:

Clone the GitHub repository, then build a local package and install it through DSH:

```bash

cd dsh-token-plugin
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-token-plugin-2.1.0.tgz

dsh-token-plugin README · Installation from this checkout：If you already have a checkout, run the last two commands from its directory. Use the package filename printed by `npm pack` if the version differs.

Restart the DSH service after installation. To install the published package, run `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-token-plugin`. Desktop recommended listings are maintained separately.

dsh-token-plugin README · What's in the package：One npm package = a **host half** (Node-side Cordis plugin: recording, billing, export — see `lib/index.js`) + a **client half** (browser-side panel — see `lib/client.js`, which talks to the host via `/usage/api`).

The package integrates with DSH through two declarations:

dsh-token-plugin README · What's in the package：| Declaration | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh.bundle.patch` (`cordis.patch.yml`) | Lets DSH recognize it as a **standard bundle plugin package**: `dsh plugin --profile <name> add <package>` installs and wires it in one command, no manual config editing |
| `dsh.client` + `exports["./client"]` | Lets the web client auto-load the browser panel at `/plugins/<package>/client.js` |

So for users, **installation is one command** — no YAML editing, no manual file copying.

dsh-token-plugin README · Updating and uninstalling：To update, pack the current checkout again and install the resulting tarball using the command above. To uninstall, run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-token-plugin` and restart DSH.

dsh-token-plugin README · Releasing (maintainers)：One command handles "bump version + test + pack":

```bash
npm run release -- patch   # 2.1.0 → 2.1.1; also minor / major / 2.2.0
```

dsh-token-plugin README · Releasing (maintainers)：The script runs the full test suite first, then writes the new version, syncs the install examples in both READMEs, turns the CHANGELOG "## 未发布 (Unreleased)" heading into the new version heading, runs the plugin contract check, and produces `dsh-token-plugin-<version>.tgz`. Add `--dry-run` to rehearse; `--no-changelog` skips the CHANGELOG heading update. It never commits, pushes, or publishes — it prints the next commands when done.

dsh-token-plugin README · Releasing (maintainers)：`npm run release:github` creates the GitHub Release and uploads the tarball from the existing tag and CHANGELOG section (requires a token in git credentials).

Local publish credentials can live in `.npmrc.local` at the repo root (gitignored, never packed); publish with `npm publish --userconfig .npmrc.local`.

dsh-token-plugin README · Data & locations：> **Since v1.9.2**, records are stored in a **fixed, dedicated data directory** (fixes [#4](https://github.com/feiyang-dev/dsh-usage-plugin/issues/4)). The path no longer follows the session workspace / `~/.dsh` / desktop-app install dir, so your history never "disappears" (counted as 0) when the workspace changes, and the path shown in the UI equals the on-disk path.

dsh-token-plugin README · Metering scope：Usage and cost here are **recorded call by call from DeepSeek Harness `llm/stream` events**, plus a `session/event` listener for search-backend requests. Read the boundaries below before relying on the numbers.

dsh-token-plugin README · Precisely metered (provider-reported values)：| Source | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Main agent conversation | Four token buckets, cache-hit counts and finish reason per call |
| Session-title generation | `purpose: session-title` |
| Context compaction | `purpose: compaction` |
| In-process subagents | They share the main agent's `ctx.llm`, so they are intercepted too |

dsh-token-plugin README · Precisely metered (provider-reported values)：The billing formula matches the official one: `uncached input × miss price + cache hit × hit price + output × output price`. There is **no separate cache-write price** (DeepSeek never reports that field; writing to cache is charged at the miss price), and `reasoning` is already included in `output`, so it is never billed twice.

dsh-token-plugin README · Not precisely metered (flagged separately in the UI)：| Source | Why it is unreachable | What the plugin does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **DeepSeek search backend calls from `web_search`** | `web-search-deepseek` issues a native `fetch` straight to `api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1/messages` inside the Harness, deliberately bypassing `ctx.llm`; upstream only persists the **request** (`web/deepseek-search-llm-request`) and **discards the response usage entirely** (its response type does not even declare a usage field). No data source exposes this spend. | Records the **exact call count** and derives a **lower bound** for the input side from the request body, all flagged `estimated`. The output side is never guessed. The overview shows "estimated cost ≥ ¥X (N calls)". |
| External CLI subagents (claude-code / codex) | Separate child processes, fully outside `ctx.llm`, emitting no events | Not counted |
| Output produced before an aborted request | The adapter emits no usage chunk on abort | Recorded as a zero-token "interrupted call" so the call count still matches the console |
| Official billing counts HTTP requests; the plugin counts streams | Harness-level retr

dsh-token-plugin README · FAQ：| Symptom | Cause / Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Panel reports `Unexpected end of JSON input` | The plugin row is missing the `inject` list, so the route isn't registered. Add the inject list per Method B3 and restart |
| Panel blank / no top tab | Plugin not activated. Check `dsh-usage-boot.log`; confirm the `cordis.patch.yml` row exists with the correct `name` |
| `dsh plugin` reports pnpm not found | Install pnpm: `npm install -g pnpm` |
| Install can't reach the npm registry | Set a mirror: `npm config set registry https://registry.npmmirror.com` (or `pnpm config set registry ...`) and retry |
| After uninstall, still reports `Cannot find package '@feiyang666/...'` | A package reference remains in the profile. Remove the corresponding row from `cordis.patch.yml` and the package name from `dsh.profile.bundles`, then restart |
| On Desktop 0.2.x every cost is ¥0 and the price page reports that all records lack a frozen unit price | 1.18.0 and earlier only recognised the provider ids `deepseek-official` / `deepseek`, while the desktop app's official-account provider id is `deepseek-account`.
